Name: empty input
Reason: input shorter than the two-byte header (PROTOCOL.md §2/§7.1)

Name: single byte, header incomplete
Reason: the header is two bytes; one byte is not a whole blob (PROTOCOL.md §2/§7.1)

Name: reserved version 2
Reason: byte 0 version bits = 10 (Reserved2); rejected before the body is read (PROTOCOL.md §2.3/§7.2)

Name: reserved version 3
Reason: byte 0 version bits = 11 (Reserved3); rejected before the body is read (PROTOCOL.md §2.3/§7.2)

Name: reserved bit set in header byte 0
Reason: byte 0 reserved bits 3-0 must be zero (PROTOCOL.md §2.1/§7.2)

Name: reserved bit set in header byte 1
Reason: byte 1 reserved bits 1-0 must be zero (PROTOCOL.md §2.2/§7.3)

Name: reserved width code
Reason: byte 1 bin-dimensions width = 10 (reserved); only codes 0 (8-bit) and 1 (16-bit) reach the wire (PROTOCOL.md §4/§7.3)

Name: body missing item count
Reason: header is valid but the body has no room for the uint16 item count (PROTOCOL.md §3/§7)

Name: truncated body ends mid-bin
Reason: header declares 1 item (all 8-bit) but the body ends after 1 of 3 bin bytes; the decoder must reject, not read past the end (PROTOCOL.md §7.1/§7.8)

Name: trailing bytes after body
Reason: header declares 0 items and a 3-byte bin, but the body carries an extra byte; a body longer than declared is rejected (PROTOCOL.md §7.8)
